title: The Spillway Stair
description: Thirty-four limestone risers in two flights connect ground to a six-metre upper terrace.

review.notes: Round 2, still close. Fixed: pilaster buttresses on the stair-side walls, varied block sizes, intermediate landings, the grey mottling is gone, localized vertical staining under the copings. Builder's close call (tread wear): at sheet and close-up resolution the treads still read as crisp new edges; the slight nosing rounding is not visible and there is no worn dip in the middle of the steps, so it does not yet count as fixed; make the wear clearly readable (deeper centre dip, chipped nosings). Not fixed: (1) the back and the far side are still a plain box wall without pilasters or structure (sheet tiles 4-5, round-1 point 3). (2) Thin blue lines show through several joints under the copings (closeup_base tile), i.e. gaps between blocks. (3) Still no broken corners and no transition into the terrain (embedded base, plants in joints).
